skill.name: alphafold-database
skill.description: Access AlphaFold protein structure predictions by UniProt ID, download coordinate files, and interpret confidence metrics for structural biology research.
skill.summary: Retrieve AlphaFold protein structures and confidence data for structural biology workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are documentation false positives from Markdown fences, public AlphaFold URLs, biological identifiers, and reference links. Two findings remain confirmed: a curl-to-bash installer in the API reference and a shell=True subprocess example that builds a gsutil command from function parameters.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into bash.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the curl-to-bash instruction and link to verified Google Cloud SDK installation steps instead.

remediation.issue: A gsutil command is constructed as a shell string and executed with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Use subprocess.run with an argument list, validate taxonomy_id as numeric, and validate output_dir before use.

remediation.issue: Download examples omit defensive request handling.
remediation.suggestion: Add timeouts, status checks, and bounded retry logic to requests examples before writing response data.

static_findings.snippet: Always cache downloaded files locally to avoid repeated downloads.

content.value_statement: Protein teams need fast access to predicted structures and confidence metrics. This skill guides AlphaFold DB queries, downloads, and interpretation workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to retrieve AlphaFold predictions with Biopython and REST API calls.
Explains downloads for mmCIF, PDB, confidence JSON, PAE JSON, and PAE images.
Interprets pLDDT and PAE metrics for confidence-aware structure analysis.
Documents Google Cloud and BigQuery access patterns for bulk structure datasets.
Provides examples for parsing coordinate files and batch processing multiple proteins.
limitations: Does not run AlphaFold prediction models or generate new structures.
Depends on public AlphaFold DB, UniProt, 3D-Beacons, Google Cloud, and Biopython availability.
Examples require users to manage local packages, bandwidth, and storage for large downloads.
AlphaFold predictions lack ligands, cofactors, post-translational modifications, and multi-chain complexes.

use_cases.title: Retrieve a Target Structure
use_cases.description: Find an AlphaFold prediction by UniProt accession and download the coordinate file for inspection.

use_cases.title: Screen Confidence Across Proteins
use_cases.description: Batch process protein accessions and summarize pLDDT confidence statistics for prioritization.

use_cases.title: Prepare Docking Inputs
use_cases.description: Download candidate target structures and identify high-confidence regions before docking workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Find One Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AlphaFold DB to find the prediction for UniProt P00520. Summarize available files and the recommended coordinate format.

prompt_templates.title: Download Confidence Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to download the mmCIF file, confidence scores, and PAE data for AlphaFold entry AF-P00520-F1.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Multiple Proteins
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a plan to analyze pLDDT confidence for UniProt IDs P00520, P12931, and P04637 using AlphaFold DB.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Bulk Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe bulk workflow for AlphaFold human proteome metadata using Google Cloud, BigQuery, caching, and rate limits.

output_examples.input: Find the AlphaFold structure for P00520.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the prediction entry, lists available coordinate and confidence files, and explains when to use mmCIF or PDB.

output_examples.input: Explain whether a predicted domain arrangement is reliable.
output_examples.output: The skill reviews pLDDT for local confidence and PAE for domain positioning confidence, then flags regions needing caution.

output_examples.input: Plan a batch analysis for several UniProt accessions.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines retrieval, caching, confidence summary statistics, error handling, and rate limiting for repeated AlphaFold queries.

best_practices: Check pLDDT and PAE before using a predicted structure in downstream analysis.
Cache downloaded files and record the AlphaFold database version for reproducible work.
Use Google Cloud or BigQuery for large datasets instead of many individual REST downloads.
anti_patterns: Treating every AlphaFold prediction as equivalent to an experimental structure.
Running bulk downloads without storage planning, rate limits, or retry handling.
Using low-confidence regions for docking, mutagenesis, or mechanism claims without validation.

faq.question: Does this skill generate new AlphaFold predictions?
faq.answer: No. It helps retrieve and interpret predictions already available in AlphaFold DB.

faq.question: Which identifier should I use first?
faq.answer: Use a UniProt accession when possible. The skill also shows how to find accessions from other protein identifiers.

faq.question: Which coordinate format is recommended?
faq.answer: mmCIF is usually recommended because it preserves metadata and supports large structures better than legacy PDB format.

faq.question: What do pLDDT scores mean?
faq.answer: pLDDT scores estimate local residue confidence. Higher values indicate more reliable local structure predictions.

faq.question: What does PAE help assess?
faq.answer: PAE helps assess confidence in relative domain positions and long-range structural arrangements.

faq.question: Can I use this for proteome-scale work?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents Google Cloud Storage and BigQuery paths for large AlphaFold DB workflows.
